fisher_cd_budget_recovery.description: Static Cobb-Douglas Fisher markets, known utility types, recover buyer budgets from observed competitive equilibrium (Table 2 budget-only CD column). Paper: 500 generated instances with parameters drawn from U[0,10] (costs U[2,20]). This gym: 100 public labeled training instances and 100 held-out test instances from a private seed, budgets/types drawn from U[0.1,10] for numerical stability.

parameter_recovery_rate.description: Share of scored-slice markets whose recovered budgets are within relative L2 error 0.1 of the generating budgets.

average_exploitability.description: Mean regret of the observed allocation-price profile under the recovered budgets.

mean_relative_l2.description: Mean relative L2 error between recovered and generating budgets. The paper reports thresholded recovery and exploitability, so the paper-reference value uses the recovery threshold epsilon=0.1 rather than a reported mean.

p90_relative_l2.description: Ninetieth-percentile relative L2 error, included to expose methods that only optimize the average case.

max_exploitability.description: Worst observed exploitability on the slice, included to penalize isolated unstable recoveries.

num_instances.description: Number of scored slice instances; informational only.

fisher_cd_noisy_budget_recovery.description: Static Cobb-Douglas Fisher markets (3 buyers, 2 goods, known types) observed through sampled behaviour: exact posted equilibrium prices and 16 independent noisy measurements of the equilibrium allocation (multiplicative log-normal noise, log-sd 0.3). Recover the buyer budgets. Tests the paper's inverse multiagent learning claim (parameters from sampled equilibrium behaviour, Corollary 1 / Section 4-5) where no exact identity pins the answer. Exploitability is measured on the true (noise-free) equilibrium under the recovered budgets. The paper reports no number for this setting: the 'results' entry is this gym's reference-method value on the held-out test split (200 instances; 200 public training instances).

parameter_recovery_rate.description: Share of held-out markets whose recovered budgets are within relative L2 error 0.1 of the generating budgets.

average_exploitability.description: Mean regret of the true (noise-free) equilibrium allocation-price profile under the recovered budgets.

mean_relative_l2.description: Mean relative L2 error between recovered and generating budgets (per-market error capped at 1).

p90_relative_l2.description: Ninetieth-percentile relative L2 error, included to expose methods that only optimize the average case.

max_exploitability.description: Worst per-market regret of the true equilibrium under the recovered budgets.

num_instances.description: Number of scored slice instances; informational only.

fisher_leontief_budget_recovery.note: Not scored. With an exact observed equilibrium and known types, every buyer's budget equals its observed expenditure p.x_i, so this setting is solved exactly by a one-line identity while the reproduced nonsmooth Algorithm 1 reached only 21% recovery (paper 36.8%); a scored copy would reward the identity, not inverse-equilibrium research. Paper numbers kept verbatim.

bertrand_cost_recovery.note: Not scored. In the homogeneous-good Bertrand duopoly the observed equilibrium price equals the marginal cost, so the answer is part of the input; every metric of the reproduced method sits exactly at its bound on both splits and cannot rank methods. Paper numbers kept verbatim.

scoring_notes: Rank = sum over experiments of weight * sum over metrics of coefficient * (candidate - reference). Per-instance relative errors are capped at 1.0 and per-instance exploitability at 100.0; a method whose predictions for an experiment are missing, duplicated, malformed, non-finite or outside the parameter domain is scored as failed on that experiment (recovery 0, every error/exploitability metric at its cap).
